chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the hand is half the wergild; and regarding the two hands together is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two feet is similar to that; and regarding the manhood when the tip is cut off, and what is above that, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the nose when the soft parts are cut off, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two lips is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two eyes is the (complete) wergild, and regarding of the two is half the wergild.

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or wergild, compensation paid for bodily injury or death
key_terms.الْحَشَفَة: The tip or glans of the male organ
key_terms.الْمَارِنُ: The soft part or cartilage of the nose

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of blood money (diyah) for specific bodily injuries like losing a hand, eye, or nose according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the foundational jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) by categorizing injuries based on symmetry and completeness, a method central to Shia legal theory. It specifically highlights the principle that bilateral injuries (like both hands or eyes) generally incur the full wergild, while unilateral losses result in half, reflecting the proportional valuation of bodily integrity in Islamic law. The detailed enumeration of specific anatomical parts, such as the *marn* of the nose and the *hushafah* of the male organ, demonstrates the precision required in applying these rulings in judicial contexts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, and Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Regarding the hand is half the wergild; and regarding the two hands together is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two feet is similar to that; and regarding the manhood when the tip is cut off, and what is above that, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the nose when the soft parts are cut off, is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two lips is the (complete) wergild; and regarding the two eyes is the (complete) wergild, and regarding of the two is half the wergild’.
